best_for: RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 owners who want to keep playing their parks on a modern Windows, Mac or Linux machine at full screen resolution.

points.title: You still need the original game
points.text: OpenRCT2 uses the graphics and music from RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 or RCT Classic, so you need one of them installed, for example from GOG or Steam. RCT1 files are optional. The original game does not have to run.

points.title: Light on hardware
points.text: It needs about 250 MB including the RCT2 files, with 1 GB free recommended, and about 500 MB of free RAM. It renders in software by default, so the CPU matters more than the graphics card; an OpenGL mode is in the options.

points.title: Supported systems
points.text: The docs list Windows 10 or later, macOS 10.13 or later, and Ubuntu 22.04 or later and Arch on Linux. If it runs slowly, lower the resolution, since it uses your screen's native resolution by default.

points.title: Release or development build
points.text: The latest release is the tested choice. Development builds carry newer features and behave like betas.

points.title: Homebrew dropped the Mac cask
points.text: Homebrew disabled its OpenRCT2 cask on 2026-09-01 because it fails Apple's Gatekeeper check. Use the universal zip listed here instead.

points.title: Installers and history
points.text: Windows gets 32-bit, x64 and Arm64 installers that install for all users. The Flathub build is verified as published by the OpenRCT2 team, for x64 and Arm64. The Windows listing keeps 44 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
